phrases.explanation: Associating partners with Allah is described as straying far from the truth. It corrupts the direction of worship and replaces the one true God with what cannot provide guidance or salvation. The distance is spiritual and moral, measured by persistent rejection of the clearest foundation of faith.

phrases.translation: Instead of Allah, they only invoke female gods and they ˹actually˺ invoke none but a rebellious Satan—
phrases.explanation: The wording refers to Arabian idols bearing female names, not to women as a class or to female spiritual worth. Invoking such idols amounts to following rebellious Satan because they cannot answer, guide, or help. The critique concerns false worship and its satanic direction, not the value of any gender.

phrases.translation: cursed by Allah
phrases.explanation: Satan is cursed by Allah, expelled and removed from His mercy because of rebellion. This description identifies the real influence behind idolatrous devotion. Calling upon powerless idols does not secure a neutral spiritual path. It aligns worshippers with the enemy who opposes Allah’s guidance. He offers no true refuge.

phrases.translation: —who said, “I will surely take hold of a certain number of Your servants
phrases.explanation: Satan vows to take an appointed share of Allah’s servants. The share consists of people who answer his call and follow his direction, not people he can forcibly own against all choice. His boast expresses hostile intention, while later verses stress that his promises cannot actually protect his followers.

phrases.translation: I will certainly mislead them and delude them with empty hopes.
phrases.explanation: Satan promises to mislead his followers and fill them with false hopes. He redirects desire away from Allah’s obedience toward fantasies of security, victory, or fulfilment through disobedience. These hopes feel attractive but lack a trustworthy foundation. His method works through invitation and deception rather than truthful guidance.

phrases.translation: Also, I will order them and they will slit the ears of cattle and alter Allah’s creation.”
phrases.explanation: Slitting cattle ears refers to pagan ritual dedication. Altering Allah’s creation was interpreted through bodily practices, but the preferred broader reading here is corrupting Allah’s religion. The context warns against satanic distortion of divine guidance, not a blanket verdict on every medical treatment or physical alteration.

phrases.translation: And whoever takes Satan as a guardian instead of Allah has certainly suffered a tremendous loss
phrases.explanation: Taking Satan as guardian instead of Allah brings clear loss because he cannot protect anyone from divine judgment. His guardianship lasts only while a person enjoys temporary respite and disappears when help is truly needed. Exchanging Allah’s reliable protection for satanic promises ends in evident ruin.

phrases.translation: Satan only makes them ˹false˺ promises and deludes them with ˹empty˺ hopes.
phrases.explanation: Satan makes promises and arouses desires that suggest he can provide support, success, and security. These appeals target imagination and longing rather than established truth. The hopes he creates distract people from Allah’s trustworthy promise and make disobedience appear beneficial despite its eventual consequences. Such hopes remain fundamentally unreliable.

phrases.translation: Truly Satan promises them nothing but delusion
phrases.explanation: Every satanic promise is delusion. When judgment arrives, Satan cannot rescue his followers and instead leaves them responsible for answering his call. His inability to fulfil his claims exposes the deception completely. Divine promises remain true, while his apparent offers of help contain no dependable substance.

phrases.translation: It is they who will have Hell as their home,
phrases.explanation: Hell is the home awaiting those who take Satan as protector instead of Allah. Their chosen guardianship cannot provide an alternative refuge when judgment comes. The destination corresponds to the false allegiance described earlier. It is not an arbitrary fate imposed without their response to deception.

phrases.translation: and they will find no escape from it
phrases.explanation: They will find no escape from Hell through satanic promises, allies, or personal schemes. The one who encouraged their rebellion cannot open a way out or protect them from Allah. Every imagined route of rescue outside divine mercy fails, exposing the complete unreliability of Satan’s guardianship.

phrases.translation: And those who believe and do good, We will soon admit them into Gardens under which rivers flow, to stay there for ever and ever.
phrases.explanation: Those who believe in Allah and His Messenger and perform righteous deeds will enter everlasting Gardens watered by rivers. Faith is joined with fulfilling obligations and avoiding wrong. Their permanent home contrasts directly with the destination of Satan’s followers and shows the lasting outcome of sincere obedience.

phrases.translation: Allah’s promise is ˹always˺ true.
phrases.explanation: Allah’s promise is true, unlike Satan’s deliberately deceptive promises. What He assures believers will happen is not a fantasy created to manipulate desire. The contrast invites trust in divine speech rather than attractive but empty hopes. Eternal reward rests upon the character of the One who promises.

phrases.translation: And whose word is more truthful than Allah’s
phrases.explanation: No one’s word is more truthful than Allah’s. He does not lie or break His promise, and He has no need to deceive anyone for benefit. This rhetorical question seals the assurance of Paradise. Believers can rely upon His declaration with greater confidence than upon any human guarantee.

phrases.translation: ˹Divine grace is˺ neither by your wishes nor those of the People of the Book!
phrases.explanation: Divine grace and judgment do not follow the wishes of Muslims, earlier scriptural communities, or idolaters. Religious labels and hopeful claims cannot determine salvation. The statement challenges every group that assumes privilege for itself. Allah’s standards are not reshaped by communal desire or self-declared spiritual status.

phrases.translation: Whoever commits evil will be rewarded accordingly,
phrases.explanation: Whoever does evil, small or great and whether believer or unbeliever, is answerable for it. This general reading rejects claims that identity cancels accountability. It does not deny the repentance and forgiveness taught elsewhere, but it makes clear that no wrong is morally erased by wishful thinking.

phrases.translation: and they will find no protector or helper besides Allah
phrases.explanation: The wrongdoer will find no protector or helper besides Allah who can shield them from His judgment. Patrons, communities, and religious leaders cannot overturn divine recompense. This removes the imagined value of group solidarity in sin and leaves each person dependent upon Allah’s justice, repentance, and mercy.

phrases.translation: But those who do good—whether male or female—and have faith will enter Paradise and will never be wronged ˹even as much as˺ the speck on a date stone
phrases.explanation: Any male or female believer who performs righteous deeds will enter Paradise and receive a full reward without the slightest reduction. Gender does not determine access to faith, moral responsibility, or divine recompense. The tiny speck on a date stone emphasizes that no good deed is diminished or ignored.

phrases.translation: And who is better in faith than those who ˹fully˺ submit themselves to Allah, do good,
phrases.explanation: No faith is better than submitting oneself fully to Allah while doing good. Submission involves the whole person, not merely verbal affiliation, and good conduct gives that devotion practical form. The combination excludes both claimed belief without obedience and outward goodness directed away from God.

phrases.translation: and follow the Way of Abraham, the upright?
phrases.explanation: True submission follows Abraham’s upright way of sincere devotion to Allah rather than idolatry. Abraham provides a model that predates later communal labels and cannot be monopolized by them. His path joins steadfast monotheism with obedience, offering a shared reference point for evaluating religious claims.

phrases.translation: Allah chose Abraham as a close friend
phrases.explanation: Allah chose Abraham as a close friend because of his sincere worship, obedience, and eagerness for divine pleasure. This honour was a gift, not payment for fulfilling a need in God. Abraham’s friendship with Allah highlights the value of devoted faith rather than ancestry or inherited religious identity.

phrases.translation: To Allah ˹alone˺ belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth.
phrases.explanation: Everything in the heavens and earth belongs to Allah. He therefore needs nothing from Abraham or any other creature, and His friendship is never motivated by lack. Every being depends upon Him instead. Divine generosity and honour flow from His grace toward creation, not from any deficiency within Him.

phrases.translation: And Allah is Fully Aware of everything
phrases.explanation: Allah encompasses and knows everything, including every good and evil deed, however small. His awareness extends throughout the dominion just described. Nothing escapes His knowledge or lies outside His judgment. This assures faithful people that obedience is seen and warns wrongdoers that no act disappears from accountability.

phrases.translation: They ask you ˹O Prophet˺ regarding women.
phrases.explanation: People asked the Prophet for guidance concerning women and their rights. The question shows that existing practices required divine correction rather than automatic acceptance. The answer directs attention away from custom and male preference toward Allah’s instruction, including matters the questioners themselves had not thought to raise.

phrases.translation: Say, “It is Allah Who instructs you regarding them.
phrases.explanation: Allah, rather than the Prophet’s personal preference, provides the authoritative instruction about women. His answer also recalls what has already been revealed, so guidance must be read together rather than treating each question as isolated. Existing revelation supplies principles and rulings that the community had neglected.

phrases.translation: Instruction has ˹already˺ been revealed in the Book concerning the orphan women you deprive of their due rights but still wish to marry, also helpless children, as well as standing up for orphans’ rights.
phrases.explanation: The verse recalls instructions on inheritance and orphan girls whose guardians denied rights while controlling marriage. Reports differ whether guardians wished to marry them or refused while retaining wealth. Both readings condemn exploiting guardianship. Helpless children and all orphans must receive justice and their appointed rights.

phrases.translation: And whatever good you do is certainly well known to Allah.”
phrases.explanation: Allah knows every good action done for women, children, and orphans, including justice that receives no public recognition. He preserves it for recompense. This assurance encourages honest care even when vulnerable people cannot repay it and warns that hidden neglect or exploitation is equally known.

phrases.translation: If a woman fears indifference or neglect from her husband, there is no blame on either of them if they seek ˹fair˺ settlement, which is best.
phrases.explanation: When a wife fears her husband’s aversion or neglect, both spouses may make a fair settlement, including a voluntary adjustment of marital rights. Reconciliation is better than separation when genuinely fair and freely accepted. The verse cannot mean pressuring a wife to surrender maintenance or accept mistreatment against her will.

phrases.translation: Humans are ever inclined to selfishness.
phrases.explanation: The statement about selfishness was applied by some to wives’ desire for full shares and by others to both spouses. It recognizes how personal claims and preferences can make compromise difficult. It should not portray women alone as selfish while ignoring a husband’s neglect or desire for advantage.

phrases.translation: But if you are gracious and mindful ˹of Allah˺, surely Allah is All-Aware of what you do
phrases.explanation: If spouses act graciously and remain mindful of Allah, He knows everything they do. Husbands are specifically urged to maintain rights and good conduct even without affection. Kindness and restraint are not wasted when unnoticed. Allah’s awareness covers both sincere generosity and concealed injustice within the marriage.

phrases.translation: You will never be able to maintain ˹emotional˺ justice between your wives—no matter how keen you are.
phrases.explanation: Complete equality of love is beyond human control, even with sincere effort. The verse addresses involuntary feelings, not permission for unequal maintenance, time, or dignity. A husband remains responsible for what he can control, and inability to feel identical love cannot justify abandoning obligations toward any wife.

phrases.translation: So do not totally incline towards one leaving the other in suspense.
phrases.explanation: In the polygamous setting, total inclination toward one wife while leaving another suspended is forbidden. A woman must not be left as though neither properly married nor free to move on. Financial support, allotted time, and respectful conduct remain obligatory regardless of where stronger affection naturally lies.

phrases.translation: And if you do what is right and are mindful ˹of Allah˺, surely Allah is All-Forgiving, Most Merciful
phrases.explanation: If spouses repair their conduct and fear Allah, He is forgiving and merciful toward earlier injustice and emotional imbalance. Repentance includes restoring practical fairness rather than merely regretting feelings. Divine mercy accompanies sincere correction, while the command to protect each wife’s rights remains fully in force.

phrases.translation: But if they choose to separate, Allah will enrich both of them from His bounties.
phrases.explanation: If reconciliation fails and the spouses separate, Allah can enrich each through provision, contentment, or a better future. The promise does not require immediate remarriage or deny the pain of divorce. It prevents either spouse from treating the marriage as their only possible source of security and sufficiency.

phrases.translation: And Allah is Ever-Bountiful, All-Wise
phrases.explanation: Allah is Ever-Bountiful and All-Wise in what He provides and decrees after separation. His bounty reaches both people rather than favouring only the husband or only the wife. His wisdom governs reconciliation and divorce alike, offering hope that a just separation need not end in lasting deprivation.

phrases.translation: To Allah ˹alone˺ belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth.
phrases.explanation: Allah owns everything in the heavens and earth, including every source of provision and companionship. Following the promise to enrich separated spouses, this ownership assures people that their security ultimately depends upon Him. No divorce, loss, or human withdrawal removes anything from His sovereign reach.

phrases.translation: Indeed, We have commanded those given the Scripture before you, as well as you, to be mindful of Allah.
phrases.explanation: Allah commanded earlier scriptural communities and the present believers alike to be mindful of Him. God-consciousness is therefore a shared obligation across revelations, not a new burden invented for one community. Every recipient of scripture is called to guard against disobeying divine commands and prohibitions.

phrases.translation: But if you disobey, then ˹know that˺ to Allah belongs whatever is in the heavens and the earth.
phrases.explanation: If people disobey or reject His command, everything in existence still belongs to Allah. Their rebellion does not reduce His dominion or make Him dependent upon their obedience. They harm themselves and invite consequences, while divine ownership and power remain completely unchanged. Human defiance cannot diminish Him in any way.

phrases.translation: And Allah is Self-Sufficient, Praiseworthy
phrases.explanation: Allah is Self-Sufficient and Praiseworthy. He needs no person’s worship, support, or resources, yet He remains worthy of praise for His favours. Obedience benefits the servant rather than supplying a deficiency in God. Gratitude and mindfulness are therefore fitting responses to His independent perfection. Praise therefore belongs to Him alone.

phrases.translation: To Allah ˹alone˺ belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth.
phrases.explanation: The repeated declaration that Allah owns the heavens and earth reinforces total divine sovereignty after the warning against disobedience. No rival owner can protect rebellion or claim an independent portion of creation. Everything people rely upon remains within the possession of the One whose commands they receive.

phrases.translation: And Allah is sufficient as a Trustee of Affairs
phrases.explanation: Allah is sufficient as Trustee of Affairs, sustaining and governing all that He owns without fatigue or loss of knowledge. Believers can entrust their concerns to Him rather than to alliances built on disobedience. His management is adequate for every matter, whether personal security, justice, or the fate of communities.

phrases.translation: If it is His Will, He can remove you altogether, O humanity,
phrases.explanation: If Allah wills, He can remove humanity entirely. Human existence depends upon His continued gift rather than an independent right to remain. This warning addresses those who imagine that their rejection weakens His religion or leaves Him needing their support. Their presence is never indispensable to Him.

phrases.translation: and replace you with others.
phrases.explanation: He can replace one people with others who will support His Prophet and obey Him. Rejection therefore cannot frustrate the divine purpose. This is a statement of God’s power, not a command for human beings to destroy or replace others. It warns against arrogance toward revelation.

phrases.translation: And Allah is Most Capable to do so
phrases.explanation: Allah is fully capable of removing and replacing people. No population size, military strength, or inherited status could prevent it. The declaration makes divine power concrete and removes any illusion that a community is too important to be held accountable for betrayal or abandonment of faith.

phrases.translation: Whoever desires the reward of this world, then ˹let them know that˺ with Allah are the rewards of this world and the Hereafter.
phrases.explanation: Those who seek only worldly returns should recognize that both worldly and lasting rewards come from Allah. Seeking His provision is better than displaying faith for spoils or safety. The verse redirects desire rather than condemning every worldly need or lawful benefit, placing all reward under His generous control.

phrases.translation: And Allah is All-Hearing, All-Seeing
phrases.explanation: Allah hears every request and sees every action and motive. He knows whether someone seeks temporary display, material gain, or lasting divine pleasure. Nothing about human ambition is hidden from Him. His hearing and sight ensure that both public achievement and private intention receive their proper recompense.

phrases.translation: O believers! Stand firm for justice as witnesses for Allah even if it is against yourselves, your parents, or close relatives.
phrases.explanation: Believers must stand firmly for justice and testify truthfully for Allah, even against themselves, parents, or close relatives. Love and loyalty cannot justify false evidence. This command directly answers attempts to defend wrongdoers through group solidarity. Justice begins where personal interest and family pressure are strongest.

phrases.translation: Be they rich or poor, Allah is best to ensure their interests.
phrases.explanation: Neither wealth nor poverty should distort testimony or judgment. Allah is nearer to both rich and poor and best knows how to protect their interests. Favouring the powerful out of greed or the poor out of partiality can still betray truth. Compassion must operate through justice rather than replace it.

phrases.translation: So do not let your desires cause you to deviate ˹from justice˺.
phrases.explanation: Personal desire must not lead believers away from fairness. Desire can appear as family loyalty, fear, sympathy, greed, or hostility. The command requires recognizing those influences before they shape evidence. Justice is an act of worship whose standard remains stable even when emotions pull toward a preferred outcome.

phrases.translation: If you distort the testimony or refuse to give it, then ˹know that˺ Allah is certainly All-Aware of what you do
phrases.explanation: Distorting testimony or refusing to provide it are both known to Allah. Twisting words can conceal truth as effectively as silence. A witness cannot escape responsibility by claiming that no explicit lie was spoken. Divine awareness covers deliberate omissions, misleading presentation, and every motive behind them.

phrases.translation: O believers! Have faith in Allah, His Messenger, the Book He has revealed to His Messenger, and the Scriptures He revealed before.
phrases.explanation: Those addressed as believers are called to complete faith in Allah, Muhammad, the Quran, and earlier scriptures. For people of earlier revelation, accepting the latest messenger is part of fidelity to their own faith. Belief is not a static label but continued acceptance of the guidance Allah sends.

phrases.translation: Indeed, whoever denies Allah, His angels, His Books, His messengers, and the Last Day has clearly gone far astray
phrases.explanation: Denying Allah, His angels, books, messengers, or the Last Day leads far astray. Selective rejection of Muhammad cannot be combined with a claim to accept revelation as a whole. The required articles form one coherent trust. Rejecting an essential part contradicts the faith professed in the remainder.

phrases.translation: Indeed, those who believed then disbelieved, then believed and again disbelieved—˹only˺ increasing in disbelief
phrases.explanation: The verse describes repeated acceptance and rejection of guidance followed by increasing disbelief. Interpretations apply it to successive rejection of Moses, Jesus, and Muhammad or to hypocrites who die in disbelief. It does not describe someone who sincerely repents and remains faithful. Accepted repentance after apostasy is explicitly affirmed elsewhere in the discussion.

phrases.translation: —Allah will neither forgive them nor guide them to the ˹Right˺ Way
phrases.explanation: Allah will not forgive or guide those who persist in this escalating rejection and remain in it. Their repeated turning away results in being left without direction toward truth. The warning concerns settled disbelief rather than a past history of failure after genuine return. Divine judgment follows the path finally pursued.

phrases.translation: Give good news of a painful punishment to hypocrites
phrases.explanation: The hypocrites are given ironic good news of a painful punishment. The wording turns the language of welcome announcement into a severe warning, exposing the dreadful outcome beneath their outward profession. It prepares for the conduct described next, especially alliances chosen against the believers and reliance upon false sources of honour.

phrases.translation: who choose disbelievers as allies instead of the believers.
phrases.explanation: These hypocrites take opposing disbelievers as protectors and intimate allies instead of believers. The issue is loyal support against the faith community, not ordinary kindness or peaceful relations with non-Muslims. Their outward profession is contradicted by where they place strategic trust and from whom they seek protection.

phrases.translation: Do they seek honour and power through that company?
phrases.explanation: The question asks whether they seek honour and power through such company. They apparently expect strength, status, and security from these alliances. The verse exposes that calculation as misguided. Influence gained through betrayal cannot provide lasting honour or protect them from the humiliation attached to their hypocrisy.

phrases.translation: Surely all honour and power belongs to Allah
phrases.explanation: All honour and power belong entirely to Allah, who grants strength or humiliation according to His will. Seeking invulnerability through allies against Him reverses the true source of security. Real honour cannot be obtained by abandoning faith, and apparent worldly influence remains dependent upon His sovereign permission.

phrases.translation: He has already revealed to you in the Book that when you hear Allah’s revelations being denied or ridiculed, then do not sit in that company unless they engage in a different topic,
phrases.explanation: When revelation is actively denied and ridiculed, believers must not willingly remain sitting in that gathering until the topic changes. Withdrawal refuses participation in the mockery. The instruction concerns knowingly staying during the abuse, not declaring every accidental encounter or unavoidable presence an act of disbelief.

phrases.translation: or else you will be like them.
phrases.explanation: Remaining willingly makes one like the mockers in disobedience, though not necessarily identical in inward belief. Silent participation can normalize contempt for revelation and share in the forbidden conduct. The warning focuses on complicity through chosen presence rather than claiming every listener holds exactly the same doctrine.

phrases.translation: Surely Allah will gather the hypocrites and disbelievers all together in Hell
phrases.explanation: Allah will gather hypocrites and disbelievers together in Hell, just as they joined in opposition to faith and support for one another. Their shared destiny reflects their chosen alliance. Outward religious identity cannot separate hidden hypocrisy from open rejection when both persist in enmity toward divine guidance.

phrases.translation: ˹The hypocrites are˺ those who wait to see what happens to you.
phrases.explanation: The hypocrites watch events rather than committing themselves sincerely. Their loyalty depends upon which side appears successful. Waiting for advantage replaces principled faith with calculation. This describes opportunism during the early conflict, not every cautious person who needs time to understand a disputed situation. Sincerity requires firmer commitment.

phrases.translation: So if Allah grants you victory, they say ˹to you˺, “Were we not on your side?”
phrases.explanation: When Allah grants the believers victory, they claim to have been on their side and seek a share of the benefit. Their declaration serves spoils and status rather than truth. Success makes them eager to display a loyalty they did not consistently show when the outcome was uncertain.

phrases.translation: But if the disbelievers have a share ˹of victory˺, they say ˹to them˺, “Did we not have the advantage over you, yet we protected you from the believers?”
phrases.explanation: When the opposing disbelievers gain an advantage, the same people claim to have supported and protected them from the believers. They change their account to suit the victorious side. The contradictory claims expose allegiance governed by worldly outcomes rather than a stable commitment to either truth or community.

phrases.translation: Allah will judge between ˹all of˺ you on the Day of Judgment.
phrases.explanation: Allah will judge between believers, hypocrites, and disbelievers on Judgment Day. His decision will separate sincere faith from opportunistic display and assign Paradise or punishment justly. Worldly victories cannot settle those hidden differences. Final judgment penetrates every shifting claim and contradictory profession of loyalty. No worldly alliance can alter it.

phrases.translation: And Allah will never grant the disbelievers a way over the believers
phrases.explanation: The statement is understood here as denying disbelievers a triumphant argument or way over believers on Judgment Day, not guaranteeing believers victory in every earthly battle. Worldly advantage can shift, as the verse acknowledges, but final judgment will not place persistent rejection above sincere faith.

phrases.translation: Surely the hypocrites seek to deceive Allah,
phrases.explanation: The hypocrites attempt to deceive Allah through outward professions and religious acts that conceal inner rejection. Their scheme treats visible conformity as sufficient protection. Although people may accept appearances, Allah knows the contradiction. Trying to fool Him reveals a fundamental failure to understand His knowledge.

phrases.translation: but He outwits them.
phrases.explanation: Allah outwits them by turning their scheme back upon them through exposure and just recompense. This is not dishonesty or uncertainty on His part. Their own deception becomes the means of their loss. Divine response perfectly answers their conduct while remaining rooted in complete knowledge and justice.

phrases.translation: When they stand up for prayer, they do it half-heartedly only to be seen by people—hardly remembering Allah at all
phrases.explanation: When they stand for prayer, they act lazily and seek public recognition while remembering Allah very little. Their worship serves safety and reputation rather than devotion. The description concerns this persistent hypocritical pattern, not every believer who experiences distraction, tiredness, or weakness in prayer. Their purpose is not worship itself.

phrases.translation: Torn between belief and disbelief—belonging neither to these ˹believers˺ nor those ˹disbelievers˺.
phrases.explanation: They waver between belief and disbelief, belonging sincerely to neither community despite moving between their outward camps. Their instability follows divided loyalty and self-interest. This is not the honest questioning of a seeker, but an entrenched attempt to gain acceptance from both sides without truthful commitment.

phrases.translation: And whoever Allah leaves to stray, you will never find for them a way
phrases.explanation: When Allah leaves such a person astray, no one else can find an alternative path to guide them. Human persuasion cannot replace divine guidance or force sincere faith. The statement does not authorize observers to declare particular strugglers abandoned by God. Ultimate guidance and abandonment remain His knowledge.

phrases.translation: O believers! Do not take disbelievers as allies instead of the believers.
phrases.explanation: Believers must not imitate the hypocrites by taking hostile disbelievers as protective allies instead of believers. The command concerns allegiance against the faith community, not normal friendship, trade, or kindness. Loyalty must not be transferred to those actively opposing the believers and seeking their religious downfall.

phrases.translation: Would you like to give Allah solid proof against yourselves
phrases.explanation: Such an alliance would give Allah clear evidence against those claiming faith while aiding His opponents. Their own conduct would testify against their profession. The rhetorical question warns that actions can become proof of divided loyalty, leaving no credible defence based on words alone. Their conduct would condemn their claims.

phrases.translation: Surely the hypocrites will be in the lowest depths of the Fire
phrases.explanation: Persistent hypocrites face the lowest depth of the Fire, a severe declaration about concealed rejection joined with deception and hostile alliance. Their outward religious participation does not lessen the wrong. The statement must be read with the explicit exception for repentance that immediately follows. Deception cannot conceal their reality.

phrases.translation: —and you will never find for them any helper—
phrases.explanation: No helper will rescue them from that punishment while they persist in hypocrisy. Their influential allies and shifting claims cannot provide defence before Allah. The absence of help exposes the emptiness of seeking power through opposing camps. Yet the next verse opens a genuine route back through repentance.

phrases.translation: except those who repent, mend their ways, hold fast to Allah, and are sincere in their devotion to Allah;
phrases.explanation: The exception covers hypocrites who repent, reform their conduct, hold firmly to Allah’s covenant, and make their religion sincere for Him. Restoration requires more than changing words. Repentance must reshape deeds, loyalty, and intention. Even the grave warning about the lowest Fire does not close this path.

phrases.translation: they will be with the believers.
phrases.explanation: Those who truly repent will be with the believers rather than remaining assigned to the company of persistent hypocrites. Their past does not permanently exclude them from faithful community and Paradise. Sincere transformation changes their standing and restores fellowship, demonstrating the concrete effect of accepted repentance.

phrases.translation: And Allah will grant the believers a great reward
phrases.explanation: Allah will grant the believers, including those restored through repentance, a great reward. The promise answers the great loss threatened earlier with great divine generosity. Ranks in Paradise are given by grace rather than withheld because of a repented past. Sincere return therefore has real and lasting hope.

phrases.translation: Why should Allah punish you if you are grateful and faithful?
phrases.explanation: Allah gains no benefit from punishing people if they become grateful and faithful. Gratitude includes recognizing His favours through repentance and sincere obedience, while faith includes accepting His Messenger and acting upon guidance. The question invites reform by rejecting the idea that God needs anyone’s suffering.

phrases.translation: Allah is ever Appreciative, All-Knowing
phrases.explanation: Allah is Appreciative and All-Knowing. He rewards gratitude and faith abundantly, while knowing every deed, intention, and hidden hypocrisy. His appreciation gives sincere obedience a value beyond human recognition. His knowledge ensures that genuine transformation is distinguished from another attempt to obtain advantage through appearances.

phrases.translation: Allah does not like negative thoughts to be voiced—except by those who have been wronged.
phrases.explanation: Allah dislikes public malicious or harmful speech, but a wronged person may report injustice, defend themselves, or appeal against the oppressor. The exception is not a general licence for gossip, slander, or unrestrained abuse. Speaking truthfully about harm differs from spreading evil for entertainment or revenge.

phrases.translation: Allah is All-Hearing, All-Knowing
phrases.explanation: Allah hears every spoken complaint and knows whether it expresses real injury, exaggeration, or malice. His hearing welcomes truthful appeal while His knowledge evaluates its content and intention. Victims are not required to pretend that wrong never happened, and speakers remain accountable for how they describe it.

phrases.translation: Whether you reveal or conceal a good or pardon an evil
phrases.explanation: Goodness may be shown openly or kept private, and a person may pardon someone who caused harm. Public gratitude, concealed charity, and restraint from permitted retaliation can all carry value. The verse encourages generosity in speech and conduct without making public display the measure of every good deed.

phrases.translation: —surely Allah is Ever-Pardoning, Most Capable
phrases.explanation: Allah is Ever-Pardoning although fully capable of punishing wrongdoing. His example gives pardon its moral force: people who are able to retaliate can instead forgive. Mercy is not weakness or lack of power. Divine capability makes His patience with disobedient servants especially generous and instructive.

phrases.translation: Surely those who deny Allah and His messengers and wish to make a distinction between Allah and His messengers,
phrases.explanation: Those who deny Allah’s messengers while claiming to believe in Allah try to separate God from the revelation He sends. Rejecting the messenger undermines acceptance of the One who chose and commissioned him. Faith cannot be reduced to a private idea of God detached from His communicated guidance.

phrases.translation: saying, “We believe in some and disbelieve in others,” desiring to forge a compromise
phrases.explanation: Claiming belief in some prophets and rejection of others creates a self-chosen middle path. Examples include denying Jesus or Muhammad while claiming Moses, or denying Muhammad while claiming Jesus. These are particular patterns, not descriptions of every Jew or Christian. Selective acceptance replaces revelation with personal preference.

phrases.translation: they are indeed the true disbelievers.
phrases.explanation: People who selectively accept some messengers while rejecting others are described as true disbelievers because their professed acceptance is incomplete and self-contradictory. Acknowledging part of revelation while denying another part does not establish faithful submission. Their own criterion is preference rather than consistent acceptance of divine guidance.

phrases.translation: And We have prepared for the disbelievers a humiliating punishment
phrases.explanation: A humiliating punishment is prepared for disbelievers who persist in this rejection. The warning concerns the Hereafter and the humiliation of discovering that selective claims offered no defence. It is not restricted to one scriptural community, but applies to anyone adopting the same pattern of denial.

phrases.translation: As for those who believe in Allah and His messengers—accepting all; rejecting none
phrases.explanation: Those who believe in Allah and all His messengers without accepting some as truthful and rejecting others as false demonstrate consistent faith. They acknowledge the truth of the guidance each messenger brought from God. This unity of acceptance contrasts with the selective compromise just condemned.

phrases.translation: —He will surely give them their rewards.
phrases.explanation: Allah will surely give such believers their rewards for affirming His messengers and the guidance they conveyed. Their recompense is promised by God rather than dependent upon public recognition. Consistent faith has lasting value even when it requires accepting a messenger opposed by one’s own community.

phrases.translation: And Allah is All-Forgiving, Most Merciful
phrases.explanation: Allah is All-Forgiving and Most Merciful, covering earlier sins for those who turn to Him in sincere faith and repentance. His mercy includes guiding people toward truth and delivering them from punishment. The promise of reward therefore does not deny their continuing need for forgiveness and grace.

phrases.translation: The People of the Book demand that you ˹O Prophet˺ bring down for them a revelation in writing from heaven.
phrases.explanation: Some People of the Book demanded that Muhammad produce a written book directly from heaven as proof. Reports describe variations of the requested sign, including writings addressed to particular individuals. The demand sets a chosen condition for belief rather than responding to the revelation already being presented.

phrases.translation: They demanded what is even greater than this from Moses, saying, “Make Allah visible to us!”
phrases.explanation: Their ancestors had made an even greater demand of Moses, asking to see Allah openly. This request exceeded the proper limits of what they could demand in worldly life. The comparison warns that escalating demands for spectacle do not necessarily produce humility or lasting faith.

phrases.translation: So a thunderbolt struck them for their wrongdoing.
phrases.explanation: A thunderbolt struck them because of their wrongdoing after that improper demand. The punishment answers their own insolence rather than an innocent desire to learn. Their story illustrates that signs cannot benefit people who approach revelation with defiance and predetermined resistance. The account therefore links the consequence directly to their deliberate wrongdoing.

phrases.translation: Then they took the calf for worship after receiving clear signs.
phrases.explanation: After clear signs had reached them, they nevertheless took the calf for worship. Visible proof did not prevent later idolatry when their commitment changed. The episode exposes the weakness of demanding further miracles while neglecting the moral response required by guidance already received. Their behaviour contradicted the evidence already given.

phrases.translation: Still We forgave them for that ˹after their repentance˺ and gave Moses compelling proof
phrases.explanation: Allah pardoned that sin after their repentance and gave Moses clear authority and compelling signs confirming his prophethood. Forgiveness followed return rather than denying the seriousness of calf worship. The conclusion joins mercy with renewed evidence, showing that failure after signs need not make sincere restoration impossible.

phrases.translation: We raised the Mount over them ˹as a warning˺ for ˹breaking˺ their covenant and said, “Enter the gate ˹of Jerusalem˺ with humility.”
phrases.explanation: The Mount was raised above them as a warning connected with accepting and fulfilling their covenant, and they were told to enter Jerusalem’s gate humbly. The account stresses submission in both action and attitude. These historical events concern particular Israelites, not an inherited trait of every later Jew.

phrases.translation: We also warned them, “Do not break the Sabbath,” and took from them a firm covenant
phrases.explanation: They were also commanded not to transgress the Sabbath, and Allah took a firm covenant that they would obey His commands and prohibitions. Sacred time and conduct were therefore matters of pledged responsibility. The firm covenant makes later violation a breach of commitment rather than simple ignorance.

phrases.translation: ˹They were condemned˺ for breaking their covenant, rejecting Allah’s signs, killing the prophets unjustly,
phrases.explanation: Condemnation is linked to breaking the covenant, rejecting Allah’s signs, and killing prophets without any right. These are specific moral crimes, not accusations based on ancestry. Prophets could not be killed legitimately for calling people to truth, and inherited scripture offered no protection against such deliberate rebellion.

phrases.translation: and for saying, “Our hearts are unreceptive!”
phrases.explanation: They claimed that their hearts were covered or unreceptive, as though inability to understand excused their rejection. The statement presents resistance as a condition they attributed to themselves. It shifts blame away from their choices rather than honestly engaging with the signs and messengers sent to them.

phrases.translation: —it is Allah Who has sealed their hearts for their disbelief,
phrases.explanation: Allah sealed their hearts because of their disbelief, making the sealing a consequence of persistent rejection rather than an arbitrary refusal to let sincere people believe. Their claimed inability becomes a judgment upon the path they chose. Divine sealing follows their culpable response to guidance.

phrases.translation: so they do not believe except for a few—
phrases.explanation: The exception concerning a few prevents an absolute ethnic or communal claim, whether understood as a small number or limited belief. The passage condemns persistent rejection by particular people while leaving room for those who sincerely believed. No one should turn it into a statement about every Jew.

phrases.translation: and for their denial and outrageous accusation against Mary
phrases.explanation: Their disbelief also included an outrageous false accusation against Mary, understood as charging her with sexual immorality without proof. The verse forcefully rejects that slander and defends her integrity. Accusing a righteous person of grave misconduct is itself a serious wrong, especially when used to discredit God’s signs.

phrases.translation: and for boasting, “We killed the Messiah, Jesus, son of Mary, the messenger of Allah.”
phrases.explanation: They boasted that they had killed the Messiah, Jesus son of Mary, while also identifying him as Allah’s messenger. The boast combines violent opposition with contempt for his mission. The coming denial answers their claim directly rather than leaving it as an uncontested historical report.

phrases.translation: But they neither killed nor crucified him—it was only made to appear so.
phrases.explanation: The verse states that they did not kill or crucify Jesus, but it was made to appear so to them. Reports differ over how the resemblance occurred, including a likeness cast on companions or on a volunteer. The verse itself does not identify the person killed, so those details remain uncertain.

phrases.translation: Even those who argue for this ˹crucifixion˺ are in doubt. They have no knowledge whatsoever—only making assumptions.
phrases.explanation: Those who disputed the event lacked certain knowledge and followed conjecture. The passage challenges confident claims based on confused reports, not historical inquiry as such. It contrasts human uncertainty about the victim with divine certainty about Jesus’ deliverance. No speculative substitute identity needs to be added to the text.

phrases.translation: They certainly did not kill him
phrases.explanation: The final categorical statement repeats that they certainly did not kill Jesus. This removes the boast’s factual foundation and affirms divine knowledge over conjecture. Repetition gives the denial deliberate emphasis. Whatever happened to the person they seized, their claim to have ended Jesus’ life is rejected.

phrases.translation: Rather, Allah raised him up to Himself.
phrases.explanation: Allah raised Jesus to Himself, affirming deliverance through divine action rather than an escape arranged by his followers. The statement does not make Jesus divine. His safety and exaltation come from God’s power and will. The immediate passage does not explain the precise mechanics of this raising.

phrases.translation: And Allah is Almighty, All-Wise
phrases.explanation: Allah is Almighty and All-Wise, able to protect His messenger despite surrounding enemies and wise in how He governs the event. Human power could not frustrate His purpose. These attributes place Jesus’ deliverance within divine sovereignty rather than chance or the effectiveness of his opponents’ plan.

phrases.translation: Every one of the People of the Book will definitely believe in him before his death.
phrases.explanation: Interpretations differ over this promise. Some place recognition before Jesus’ eventual death after his return, others before each scriptural person’s death, and another reading concerns Muhammad. A preferred explanation is belief in Jesus before his own death. The wording should not be treated as one uncontested timetable.

phrases.translation: And on the Day of Judgment Jesus will be a witness against them
phrases.explanation: On Judgment Day, Jesus will bear witness concerning the People of the Book, including denial of him and acceptance of the message he brought from Allah. His testimony concerns his mission and their response. He serves as God’s witness, not as an independent divine judge replacing Allah.

phrases.translation: We forbade the Jews certain foods that had been lawful to them for their wrongdoing,
phrases.explanation: Certain previously lawful good foods were forbidden to particular Israelites as a consequence of their wrongdoing. The restriction is presented as disciplinary judgment, not proof that the foods were inherently impure or that every dietary rule has the same cause. The verse continues recounting historical covenant violations.

phrases.translation: and for hindering many from the Way of Allah
phrases.explanation: They also hindered many from Allah’s way through false claims, distortion of scripture, and concealment of guidance, including knowledge about Muhammad. Obstructing others compounds personal rejection. The punishment therefore responds not only to inward disbelief, but also to active efforts that turned people away from truth.

phrases.translation: taking interest despite its prohibition, and consuming people’s wealth unjustly.
phrases.explanation: The list adds prohibited interest, described as demanding an increase for delayed repayment, and consuming wealth through bribes or fabricated religious claims. These are concrete economic and religious injustices. The passage condemns particular offenders rather than authorizing a blanket charge against every member of their community.

phrases.translation: We have prepared for the disbelievers among them a painful punishment
phrases.explanation: A painful punishment is prepared for those among them who persist in disbelief. The wording restricts the threat to a described group rather than everyone sharing their ancestry. The next verse makes the distinction even clearer by promising a great reward to well-grounded, faithful people among them.

phrases.translation: But those of them well-grounded in knowledge, the faithful ˹who˺ believe in what has been revealed to you ˹O Prophet˺ and what was revealed before you—˹especially˺ those who establish prayer
phrases.explanation: Well-grounded people of knowledge and the faithful are explicitly excepted. They believe in what was revealed to Muhammad and in earlier revelation, joining learning with acceptance rather than using scholarship to resist truth. Their example proves that the preceding condemnation was never an indiscriminate description of an entire community.

phrases.translation: —and those who pay alms-tax and believe in Allah and the Last Day, to these ˹people˺ We will grant a great reward
phrases.explanation: They also establish prayer, give alms, and believe in Allah and the Last Day, and they will receive a great reward. Knowledge must therefore issue in worship, generosity, and accountability. The promised recompense honours sincere faith and practice wherever they appear, including among people of earlier scripture.

phrases.translation: Indeed, We have sent revelation to you ˹O Prophet˺ as We sent revelation to Noah and the prophets after him.
phrases.explanation: Muhammad receives revelation just as Noah and the prophets after him did. His mission belongs to the same divine pattern rather than arising without precedent. The comparison answers denial of revelation to a human being and confirms continuity between his message and the long history of prophethood.

phrases.translation: We also sent revelation to Abraham, Ishmael, Isaac, Jacob, and his descendants, ˹as well as˺ Jesus, Job, Jonah, Aaron, and Solomon.
phrases.explanation: The named recipients include Abraham, Ishmael, Isaac, Jacob, tribal prophets, Jesus, Job, Jonah, Aaron, and Solomon. Their diverse lives share one source of guidance. Listing them shows that no single lineage can monopolize revelation and that Muhammad’s message continues a broad prophetic tradition. All served the same divine source.

phrases.translation: And to David We gave the Psalms
phrases.explanation: David was given the Psalms, a known book of divine revelation. Mentioning his scripture alongside the prophets reinforces that earlier communities possessed genuine guidance from Allah. The Quran does not treat all earlier revelation as human invention, while calling people to accept the revelation now given to Muhammad.

phrases.translation: There are messengers whose stories We have told you already and others We have not.
phrases.explanation: Some messengers’ stories have already been told to the Prophet, while others have not been related. The list is therefore not a complete inventory of everyone Allah sent. This limitation encourages humility about unknown prophetic history and prevents treating the named figures as the only legitimate messengers.

phrases.translation: And to Moses Allah spoke directly
phrases.explanation: Allah spoke directly to Moses in true address, giving him a distinctive honour among the examples. The statement affirms real communication from God rather than reducing revelation to Moses’ private thoughts. It does not make Moses divine or remove his status as a servant and messenger.

phrases.translation: ˹All were˺ messengers delivering good news and warnings so humanity should have no excuse before Allah after ˹the coming of˺ the messengers.
phrases.explanation: The messengers brought good news of reward for faith and obedience and warnings of punishment for rejection. Their missions gave people clear direction and removed the excuse that no guide had come. After receiving their message, denial becomes a response to communicated truth rather than simple absence of information.

phrases.translation: And Allah is Almighty, All-Wise
phrases.explanation: Allah is Almighty and All-Wise in sending messengers and establishing accountability. His power ensures that His purpose cannot be defeated, and His wisdom governs both guidance and judgment. Humanity’s inability to claim ignorance rests upon His deliberate and effective communication through the prophetic missions. His guidance is never purposeless.

phrases.translation: Yet ˹if you are denied, O Prophet,˺ Allah bears witness to what He has sent down to you
phrases.explanation: Even if people deny Muhammad, Allah Himself bears witness to the revelation He sent to him. Human rejection cannot overturn divine testimony. This directly answers those demanding a different heavenly book or claiming that God sends nothing to human beings. The Prophet’s confidence rests upon God’s confirmation.

phrases.translation: —He has sent it with His knowledge.
phrases.explanation: Allah sent the revelation with His knowledge, choosing His trusted messenger and knowing the content and purpose of what was revealed. The mission is neither accidental nor based on Muhammad’s private guessing. Divine knowledge stands behind both the message and the selection of its recipient.

phrases.translation: The angels too bear witness.
phrases.explanation: The angels also bear witness to the revelation and the Prophet’s truthfulness. Their testimony adds a further dimension beyond hostile human accusations. The Prophet is therefore not dependent upon recognition from those who reject him, however learned or influential those opponents appear. Their witness confirms what opponents deny.

phrases.translation: And Allah ˹alone˺ is sufficient as a Witness
phrases.explanation: Allah alone is sufficient as Witness. If His testimony establishes the Prophet’s truthfulness, no denial can genuinely harm that status. Additional witnesses do not fill a deficiency in His evidence. The statement offers reassurance that rejection by people cannot outweigh confirmation from God. His verdict needs no human majority.

phrases.translation: Those who disbelieve and hinder ˹others˺ from the Way of Allah have certainly strayed far away
phrases.explanation: Those who disbelieve and also hinder others from Allah’s way stray far from guidance. Their wrong includes misleading inquirers and concealing what they know about the Messenger. Personal rejection is compounded by obstructing other people. The passage concerns deliberate opposition, not sincere uncertainty or peaceful discussion of belief.

phrases.translation: Those who disbelieve and wrong themselves—surely Allah will neither forgive them nor guide them to any path
phrases.explanation: Those who persist in knowing disbelief and wrong themselves through injustice will not be forgiven or guided toward a saving path while remaining in that state. Their own persistent choices close the route they refuse. The warning concerns settled rejection and wrongdoing rather than someone sincerely returning in repentance.

phrases.translation: except that of Hell, to stay there for ever and ever.
phrases.explanation: The only path left for persistent rejecters is Hell, where they remain forever. The statement continues the severe warning about final, unrepented disbelief and wrongdoing. It does not invite humans to assign that destiny to particular people, since Allah alone knows who ultimately persists without repentance.

phrases.translation: And that is easy for Allah
phrases.explanation: Carrying out that judgment is easy for Allah. No opponent can resist His decision or prevent its execution. Divine power requires no struggle to fulfil justice. The closing statement removes any thought that human influence, concealment, or collective support could make final accountability too difficult to enforce.

phrases.translation: O humanity! The Messenger has certainly come to you with the truth from your Lord,
phrases.explanation: All humanity is addressed with the declaration that Muhammad has brought truth from their Lord. The invitation extends beyond one tribe or earlier scriptural community. His message presents itself as divine guidance for everyone, so the response cannot be dismissed as a matter concerning only his immediate listeners.

phrases.translation: so believe for your own good.
phrases.explanation: People are told to believe because faith is better for them. Acceptance benefits the person who responds through guidance and eventual reward, rather than supplying anything Allah lacks. The command therefore appeals to human welfare and invites a choice grounded in truth, not service to divine need.

phrases.translation: But if you disbelieve, then ˹know that˺ to Allah belongs whatever is in the heavens and the earth.
phrases.explanation: If people disbelieve, everything in the heavens and earth still belongs to Allah. Their rejection does not diminish His kingdom or harm His messenger’s divine source. They bear the loss themselves. God’s ownership remains complete whether every individual accepts the message or turns away from it.

phrases.translation: And Allah is All-Knowing, All-Wise
phrases.explanation: Allah knows every response and is wise in every command, prohibition, and judgment. He knows who accepts, rejects, or obstructs guidance, and nothing is hidden from Him. His wisdom assures that the invitation and its consequences serve truth and justice rather than arbitrary favour toward one community.

phrases.translation: O People of the Book! Do not go to extremes regarding your faith;
phrases.explanation: The People of the Gospel are told not to exceed proper bounds in religion through exaggerated claims about Jesus. Honouring a messenger must not turn him into another divine lord. Excess is measured against truth, not against love or respect. Faithful devotion requires remaining within what Allah has actually revealed.

phrases.translation: say nothing about Allah except the truth.
phrases.explanation: Nothing should be said about Allah except the truth. Religious emotion, inherited teaching, or reverence for a holy person cannot justify false claims about God’s nature. Theological speech requires restraint and fidelity to revelation. This command governs both excessive praise and accusations that contradict divine guidance.

phrases.translation: The Messiah, Jesus, son of Mary, was no more than a messenger of Allah and the fulfilment of His Word through Mary and a spirit ˹created by a command˺ from Him.
phrases.explanation: Jesus is Mary’s son and Allah’s messenger, called His word through the announcement to Mary and creation by divine command. A spirit from Him has several interpretations, including created life or mercy, all pointing to divine origination rather than a fragment of God. These honours do not make him Allah’s son.

phrases.translation: So believe in Allah and His messengers and do not say, “Trinity.”
phrases.explanation: Belief in Allah and His messengers is required, while saying Trinity in the sense of three divine lords is rejected. The verse does not analyze every detailed Christian formulation. Its central correction is exclusive worship of one God without partner or child, alongside genuine honour for Jesus as messenger.

phrases.translation: Stop!—for your own good.
phrases.explanation: The command to stop is urgent and for the audience’s own good. Abandoning false claims is better than persisting toward punishment. The wording offers a corrective route rather than expressing hatred toward Jesus or his followers. Ceasing theological excess protects both true monotheism and the proper honour due to messengers.

phrases.translation: Allah is only One God.
phrases.explanation: Allah is only one God, without partner, consort, parent, or child. Exclusive divinity belongs to Him alone. This declaration directly answers any attempt to place another lord beside Him. Worship and sovereignty cannot be divided among Jesus, Mary, angels, or any other created being. He alone deserves all worship.

phrases.translation: Glory be to Him! He is far above having a son!
phrases.explanation: Allah is exalted far above having a son. This denies divine sonship, not Jesus’ miraculous creation or honoured status. God’s perfection includes no need, reproduction, or lineage. The statement also rejects any implication that He physically fathered a child through Mary. His uniqueness admits no such biological relationship.

phrases.translation: To Him belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth.
phrases.explanation: Everything in the heavens and earth belongs to Allah, including Jesus, Mary, and the angels. They are created, sustained, and dependent upon Him rather than independent divine beings. Universal ownership answers claims of divine sonship by placing every honoured servant firmly within God’s creation. Their dependence upon Him is complete.

phrases.translation: And Allah is sufficient as a Trustee of Affairs
phrases.explanation: Allah is sufficient as Trustee of Affairs, sustaining and governing everything without needing a son, partner, or assistant. His complete management leaves no deficiency that another divine figure must fill. Creation can rely upon Him directly, while every created messenger remains under His authority and care.

phrases.translation: The Messiah would never be too proud to be a servant of Allah,
phrases.explanation: The Messiah does not disdain being Allah’s servant. His honoured mission therefore provides no basis for treating him as a divine being who stands outside servitude. Accepting Jesus includes accepting his submission to God. True greatness does not make worship beneath him. Servitude belongs to his actual mission and example.

phrases.translation: nor would the angels nearest to Allah.
phrases.explanation: Even the angels nearest to Allah do not reject servitude, although their ranks are exalted. Their example reinforces that closeness to God increases devotion rather than independence. If Jesus and the highest angels worship, no human being can reasonably claim that humble service is beneath their dignity.

phrases.translation: Those who are too proud and arrogant to worship Him will be brought before Him all together
phrases.explanation: Those who disdain worship and become arrogant will all be gathered before Allah. Pride cannot exempt anyone from resurrection or accountability. Their attempted independence ends when they stand in His presence. The warning applies to every creature who refuses servitude, not only to people holding one particular doctrine.

phrases.translation: As for those who believe and do good, He will reward them in full and increase them out of His grace.
phrases.explanation: Those who believe and do righteous deeds will receive their rewards in full and an additional increase from Allah’s bounty. Nothing earned is reduced, while further grace remains unlimited by human calculation. The promise joins perfect justice with generosity beyond strict entitlement. Faithful humility therefore leads to abundance rather than loss.

phrases.translation: But those who are too proud and arrogant, He will subject them to a painful punishment.
phrases.explanation: Those who consider themselves too great for worship and persist in arrogance will receive a painful punishment. Their attitude rejects the fundamental relationship between Creator and servant. The contrast with rewarded believers shows that the issue is not intelligence or status, but proud refusal to obey.

phrases.translation: And besides Allah they will find no protector or helper
phrases.explanation: They will find no protector or helper besides Allah to rescue them from His punishment. Status, angels, messengers, and powerful allies cannot be used as shields against accountability. Assistance sought from created beings cannot overturn divine judgment. Deliverance requires returning to Allah rather than relying upon another patron.

phrases.translation: O humanity! There has come to you conclusive evidence from your Lord.
phrases.explanation: All humanity has received conclusive evidence from its Lord, identified with Muhammad’s confirmed prophethood and message. The proof addresses the different communities discussed throughout the chapter and removes the excuse of having no clear guide. Divine evidence calls for a response rather than passive admiration.

phrases.translation: And We have sent down to you a brilliant light
phrases.explanation: Allah has also sent a clear light, the revelation that illuminates the path toward truth and deliverance. Light makes guidance visible so people can distinguish direction from error. Its clarity does not compel belief, but it allows those willing to follow it to see where salvation lies.

phrases.translation: As for those who believe in Allah and hold fast to Him, He will admit them into His mercy and grace and guide them to Himself through the Straight Path
phrases.explanation: Those who believe in Allah and hold fast to Him and His clear revelation will enter His mercy and bounty and be guided along the Straight Path. Holding fast implies persevering commitment rather than momentary acknowledgement. Guidance, mercy, and reward all come from Allah, leading believers toward Him without deviation.

phrases.translation: They ask you ˹for a ruling, O Prophet˺.
phrases.explanation: People asked the Prophet for an inheritance ruling, and Allah supplied the answer. The question concerns a specific family situation that needed clarification beyond the shares given earlier. Seeking guidance rather than relying upon custom protects property rights and prevents surviving relatives from inventing convenient distributions.

phrases.translation: Say, “Allah gives you a ruling regarding those who die without children or parents.”
phrases.explanation: The ruling concerns someone who dies without a surviving child or parent, leaving siblings to inherit in the cases described. This definition is essential because children and parents change the distribution. The verse must not be applied to an estate with those closer heirs as though they were absent.

phrases.translation: If a man dies childless and leaves behind a sister, she will inherit one-half of his estate,
phrases.explanation: If a man dies childless in this stated case and leaves one qualifying sister, she inherits half of his estate. This is not a universal rule that every sister always receives half. The surrounding no-child, no-parent context and the presence of other eligible heirs must guide its application.

phrases.translation: whereas her brother will inherit all of her estate if she dies childless.
phrases.explanation: The reciprocal case concerns a sister dying without a child or parent and leaving the qualifying brother, who inherits her estate under that arrangement. It does not mean every brother automatically takes everything whenever a sister dies. Different surviving heirs can create a different legal case.

phrases.translation: If this person leaves behind two sisters, they together will inherit two-thirds of the estate.
phrases.explanation: Two qualifying sisters share two-thirds together, not two-thirds each. The rule continues the same no-child, no-parent context and addresses their collective portion. It complements the single sister’s half rather than contradicting it. Other heirs must still be considered before describing the complete distribution of an estate.

phrases.translation: But if the deceased leaves male and female siblings, a male’s share will be equal to that of two females.
phrases.explanation: When eligible siblings include brothers and sisters, each male receives the share of two females under this inheritance rule. This is a specified distribution for siblings in the stated case, not a declaration that men have twice women’s moral worth. The same passage assigns women substantial and enforceable property rights.

phrases.translation: Allah makes ˹this˺ clear to you so you do not go astray.
phrases.explanation: Allah explains these shares clearly so that people do not go astray in inheritance. Precision prevents guesswork, favouritism, and accidental deprivation of relatives. The detailed fractions are guidance to be followed carefully rather than problems to solve through personal preference. Clarity serves both family justice and religious obedience.

phrases.translation: And Allah has ˹perfect˺ knowledge of all things
phrases.explanation: Allah knows all things, including family circumstances and the interests affected by inheritance. His knowledge grounds these detailed rules and closes the chapter’s legal instruction with divine authority. No heir can claim a better understanding than the One who apportioned the shares and knows every consequence.
